title: Equivalence invariance of comma contractibility
statement: Use the universes and essential smallness of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] and the coherent functors, functor equivalences, mapping spaces and weak contractibility of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a coherent functor $u:I\to J$ between quasicategories and an object $j\in J$, write $(j\downarrow u)$ for the simplicial pullback $\{j\}\times_{J,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,J)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,J}I$, the coherent comma quasicategory of pairs $(i,j\to u(i))$ with all higher simplices. Let $u:I\to J$ be a coherent functor between quasicategories fitting in the larger universe, such that $(j\downarrow u)$ is weakly contractible for every $j\in J$, and let $e:I_0\to I$ and $w:J\to J_0$ be functor equivalences of quasicategories. Then $(j_0\downarrow wue)$ is weakly contractible for every $j_0\in J_0$. In particular, taking $u$ to be an identity functor, every comma quasicategory $(j\downarrow e)$ of a functor equivalence $e:I_0\to J$ is weakly contractible. No smallness of $I$, $J$, $I_0$ or $J_0$ in the smaller universe is assumed.

source.place: Section 4.1.1 (categorical equivalences are cofinal; cofinality is stable under composition) with Theorem 4.1.3.1 (comma criterion); equivalently Kerodon Theorem 7.2.3.1 and the invariance of right cofinality under equivalences. Read online; not archived in literature/. Narrowed by the maintainer reader: the comma criterion itself is lem-coef-infinity-cofinality-space-test.

proof.text: Choose a universe $\mathcal V$ containing the simplicial sets $I,J,I_0,J_0$, all the displayed functors and their quasi-inverse data; enlarge further for categories of diagrams. They are now $\mathcal V$-small, although they need not be $\mathcal U$-small. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cofinality-space-test] with its fixed universe taken to be $\mathcal V$. Its comma in condition (3) is exactly the degreewise pullback displayed in this statement, not the core of that pullback. The hypothesis and implication (3)$\Rightarrow$(1) therefore make $u$ final: for every $D:J\to\mathcal E$ and every given colimiting cocone on $D$, restriction to $I$ is colimiting. The auxiliary category of spaces in that criterion is formed using $\mathcal V$, not the original smaller universe.

source.place: Remark 7.2.3.2(2′), Theorem 7.2.3.1(2), and Proposition 7.4.3.11(1)-(2); agent-explicit universe enlargement

proof.text: For any functor equivalence $a:A\to B$ between $\mathcal V$-small quasicategories, choose its stipulated quasi-inverse $b:B\to A$ and coherent natural equivalences $ba\simeq1_A$, $ab\simeq1_B$. For every quasicategory $\mathcal E$ in a containing universe, restriction gives simplicial functors $a^*:\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal E)$ and $b^*$ in the opposite direction. Their composites send $H:A\to\mathcal E$ to $Hba$ and $D:B\to\mathcal E$ to $Dab$. The evaluation map sends $ba\simeq1_A$ to $Hba\simeq H$ and $ab\simeq1_B$ to $Dab\simeq D$, naturally in all simplices of $H,D$: explicitly evaluate a diagram on the map $A\times\Delta^1\to A$ or $B\times\Delta^1\to B$ representing the given transformation, and curry. Evaluate their inverse transformations and two inverse-triangle simplices in the same way. These give coherent inverse-triangle witnesses in the functor categories, so $a^*$ and $b^*$ are functor equivalences by definition. The functor-category and mapping-space assertions of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] apply; in particular, $a^*$ induces equivalences on mapping spaces. This construction uses the actual coherent quasi-inverse data, not an equivalence merely of homotopy categories.

source.place: Lecture II, basic facts (1), (3), (6)-(7), printed pp.14-15; agent-written currying of the given inverse data

proof.text: Let $D:B\to\mathcal E$ and let $\lambda:D\to\Delta_B L$ be a given colimiting cocone. The dual mapping-space criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] says that, for each $T\in\mathcal E$, postcomposition with $\lambda$ gives an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(L,T)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal E)}(D,\Delta_B T)$. By step 2, restriction along $a$ gives an equivalence from this latter mapping space to $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal E)}(Da,\Delta_A T)$. Their composite is the map associated to the restricted cocone: a morphism $h:L\to T$ is sent first to $(\Delta_B h)\lambda$ and then to $(\Delta_A h)(\lambda a)$, since restriction is precomposition and $a^*\Delta_B=\Delta_A$. The same equality is evaluation on simplices, so it includes the compatibility homotopies. The dual criterion now shows that $\lambda a$ is colimiting, with its original vertex $L$. Thus every functor equivalence $a$ is final under definition (1) of [lem-coef-infinity-cofinality-space-test]. No existence of other colimits in $\mathcal E$ was used.

source.place: Proposition 7.4.3.11, universal existing-colimit condition; agent proof from the cited cocone mapping-space criterion

proof.text: Apply step 3 to $w:J\to J_0$ and $e:I_0\to I$. To check finality of $wue$, take any $D:J_0\to\mathcal E$ with a given colimiting cocone $\lambda$. Restrict it first along $w$, next along $u$ using step 1, and last along $e$. The three resulting cocones $\lambda w$, $(\lambda w)u$, and $((\lambda w)u)e$ are colimiting by the definition of finality; the last is exactly $\lambda(wue)$ with the same vertex, because precomposition is associative on simplicial maps. This proves condition (1) for $wue$. Implication (1)$\Rightarrow$(3) of [lem-coef-infinity-cofinality-space-test], in universe $\mathcal V$, gives weak contractibility of the specified $(j_0\downarrow wue)$ for each $j_0\in J_0$.

source.place: Remark 7.2.3.2(2′) and Proposition 7.4.3.11; composition written directly from the universal-colimit condition

proof.text: For the last assertion, identity restriction leaves every diagram and its cocone unchanged, so $1_J$ is final by condition (1) of [lem-coef-infinity-cofinality-space-test]. Condition (3) then makes each $(j\downarrow1_J)$ weakly contractible. Apply the result of step 4 with $u=1_J$, $w=1_J$, and the given equivalence $e:I_0\to J$. Its conclusion is precisely weak contractibility of $(j\downarrow e)$ for every $j\in J$. This also covers the empty $J$ case, where there are no such vertices.

source.place: Remark 7.2.3.2(2′), specialized to identity restriction and then to the given equivalence
